name: Harvest Roast Turkey with Homemade Gravy

instructions.primary_message: FOR THE ROAST TURKEY: If using a frozen turkey, thaw in the fridge for 2-3 days. If using a fresh turkey, skip this step.
instructions.secondary_message: 5.44 kg whole turkey, fresh or frozen

instructions.primary_message: About 4 hours before you plan to serve the turkey, set it on the counter and allow to come to room temperature for 1 hour.
Once the turkey has come to room temperature, preheat oven to 325°F. Place oven rack in the lower position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ small pkg fresh rosemary
½ small pkg fresh sage
½ small pkg fresh thyme
1 lemon
1 Gala apple
1 pear

instructions.primary_message: Small dice butter and place in a small bowl along with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup butter, unsalted
1 tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the butter.
Remove half of the herbs (rosemary, sage, and thyme) from stems and mince the leaves; add to the bowl. (Reserve remaining herbs, still on their stems, for later use.)
Zest lemon into the bowl and set aside for the butter to soften.
Quarter lemon and place in another small bowl.
Quarter and core apple and pear. Add both to the bowl with the lemon.
Peel, halve, and quarter onion; add to the bowl and set aside.
Remove neck and giblets from inside the turkey (if there are any) and discard. Pat turkey dry with paper towels and place in a roasting pan.
Stuff the fruit and onion quarters inside the turkey along with the reserved herb sprigs.
Using the back of a spoon, mash the butter mixture to combine.

Using your fingers, loosen and lift the skin away from the meat of the turkey breasts and thighs. Stuff the openings with about 2/3 of the herb butter and press the skin to spread it out evenly over the meat.
Arrange the turkey breast-side up in the roasting pan. Spread and pat remaining butter over the skin of the breast and legs.
Place turkey in the oven and roast until the skin starts to turn golden, about 1 ½ hours.
Once the skin is golden, loosely cover the turkey with a piece of aluminum foil and continue to roast until the middle of a thigh or breast reaches 165°F, about 1 hour.
When the turkey is done, remove from the oven and transfer to a platter. Set aside to rest, still covered with foil, for 30 minutes.
FOR THE GRAVY: While the roast turkey is resting, carefully pour the drippings from the roasting pan into a medium bowl. Set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Once the drippings have cooled, use a spoon or ladle to skim off and discard any fat that has settled on top.
Place 1 cup of the de-fatted drippings in a medium saucepan. Add flour and whisk to combine a smooth, thin paste.
Set the pan over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat.

Add broth, salt, and pepper to the pan and whisk to combine. Return to medium-high heat and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat and continue to cook, stirring often, until gravy is thickened and flavors blend, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
710 ml chicken or vegetable broth
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: If the gravy is too thin, combine water and cornstarch in another small bowl. Add to the pan, 1 tablespoon at a time, whisking well after each addition, until the gravy reaches desired thickness.
